query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of Cr to the NbMoTaW alloy will improve its room-temperature ductility while maintaining its high-temperature mechanical performance and irradiation tolerance.
generation.intervention: Addition of Cr to the alloy
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable BCC phase with improved ductility
generation.mechanism: The addition of Cr will act as a stabilizer for the BCC phase at high contents, promoting the modulation of mechanical properties and improving room-temperature ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature ductility and maintained high-temperature mechanical performance and irradiation tolerance
generation.boundary: Temperature range: up to 1600 °C; Irradiation conditions: helium implantation and self-healing behavior
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Cr to be added and the potential formation of precipitates or phase separations

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Cr does not improve room-temperature ductility or compromises high-temperature mechanical performance and irradiation tolerance, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: W-based refractory HEAs (RHEAs) have been recently developed in the context of high-temperature applications, showing high melting temperature (above 2873 K) and superior mechanical strength at high temperatures compared to Ni-based superalloys or pure W,. Combining the two approaches above, the authors have recently developed a refractory low-activation HEA based on W-Ta-Cr-V. Its response to loop formation under ion irradiation and He implantation is enhanced compared to previously developed W-based alloys, showing no noticeable dislocation loop formation and smaller He bubbles with no radiation-induced segregation at grain boundaries upon heavy ion irradiation and He implantation, respectively. However, this quaternary RHEA demonstrated Cr- and V-rich precipitates which could be detrimental to mechanical properties in terms of embrittlement. In this study, a design strategy to further improve the overall response of the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA is introduced and resulted in the development of a quinary RHEA with improved resistance to high-temperature and irradiation environments. Developing lightweight alloys with excellent strength and ductility is always the objective for the application of structural alloys due to the demand for high-performance superalloys in increased harsh working conditions. High-entropy alloys (HEAs) and multiprincipal element alloys have received considerable interest for community experts and have become a worldwide hot spot since Cantor and Yeh reported their first publication [,]. Cr-containing HEAs have exhibited promising potential when applied in high-temperature industrial fields as a result of their remarkable strength [,,,], favorable ductility [,,], distinguished corrosion resistance [,,], superior wear and oxidation resistance [,,], and acceptable thermal stability [,]. So far, great endeavors have been devoted to examining the properties of Cr-containing HEAs with the incorporation of the Cr element, not limited to the investigations of corrosion behavior, high-temperature oxidation behavior, and thermal stability of the HEAs, especially regarding the evolution of the microstructure and mechanical behavior with different Cr content, is still a top research priority.
